claims.text: The initial material is a non-equilibrium, metastable single-phase solid solution with a uniform elemental distribution and no significant intermetallic precipitation.
Thermal exposure drives diffusion-mediated phase separation in the metastable Mg-containing alloy.
Mg-rich intermetallic compounds nucleate and grow primarily at grain boundaries, as well as within the matrix.
Reported Mg-Ti-Zn multi-principal-element alloys form intermetallic phases, including Ti2Zn and Mg21Zn25.
The size, morphology, coherence, and connectivity of the intermetallic precipitates evolve with thermal-treatment severity.
A fine, coherent intermetallic dispersion facilitates formation of a continuous protective oxide or passivation film.
A TiO2-rich surface film can enhance passivation and lower corrosion current density in a Ti-containing Mg alloy.
The cited Mg-Ti-Zn alloys exhibit good corrosion resistance in NaCl solution.
Fine and coherent intermetallics retain both corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Excessive intermetallic coarsening and discontinuous grain-boundary segregation compromise protective-film integrity.
Compromising the protective film increases oxidation kinetics and corrosion rates.
Moderate heat treatment that produces a fine, uniform intermetallic dispersion will maintain or enhance corrosion and oxidation resistance relative to the initial state.
Extended or higher-temperature treatment will cause pronounced intermetallic coarsening and grain-boundary segregation.
Temperatures of approximately 800–1000 °C define the relevant high-temperature service regime for the proposed alloy.
Corrosion behavior will be evaluated in chloride-containing media, specifically 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
Intermetallic morphology and coherence, oxidation mass gain and oxide composition, corrosion current density, and pitting potential are measurable discriminators between the treatments.

The hypothesis is falsified if samples with different intermetallic morphologies show no significant differences in oxide-scale integrity, oxidation rate, or corrosion resistance relative to the initial state.
